content.rendered:
From the 1995 opening concert for the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame: Chuck Berry backed by Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band.

“Johnny B. Goode,” of course, is one of the most recognizable songs in rock and roll. Chuck Berry’s original version from 1958 peaked at #8 on the Billboard Hot 100, but it went on to be covered by scores of artists and ranks seventh in Rolling Stone’s 500 Greatest Songs of All Time.

Johnny B. Goode
First performed: April 28, 1973 (College Park, MD)
Last performed: April 21, 2017 (Asbury Park, NJ)

© January 22, 2018

jetpack-related-posts.title: Bye Bye Johnny
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Chuck Berry's "Bye Bye Johnny" inspired one of Bruce's own songs, but strangely he's only covered it a few times. Here's his most recent performance, with Little Steven and the Disciples of Soul.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Around and Around
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Many, many times--but almost always in small clubs: Bruce rocks the house with a cover of Chuck Berry's classic B-side, "Around and Around."

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rock and Roll Music
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce leads an all-star line-up on a raucous cover of Chuck Berry's "Rock and Roll Music."

jetpack-related-posts.title: Shake, Rattle and Roll
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A rusty E Street Band lumbered through their first attempt at Big Joe Turner's rock and roll standard, but they more than made up for it 18 years later.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Johnny Bye Bye
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: An early rock and roll sequel and the tragic deaths of two of his musical heroes inspired this powerful, under-the-radar B-side.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hard Travelin’
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce helped launch the American Music Masters series by leading an all-star encore of one of Woody Guthrie's most-recorded songs.
